Here we have two nitrogens in the ring? `N[C@H]1CCCCN(...)C1` implies a diazine or diazepane? Let's count atoms: N-C-C-C-C-N-C -> 7 membered ring? Or maybe it's a piperazine? `N1CCCCN1` is piperazine. But there's a chiral center `[C@H]1`. So it's likely a substituted piperazine or azepane. Actually, `N[C@H]1CCCCN(C(=O)OCc2ccccc2)C1` could be a piperazine derivative where one N is part of the ring and the other is exocyclic? No, `N[C@H]1` means the N is attached to the chiral C which starts the ring. So it's `Boc-N-CH-CH2-CH2-CH2-CH2-N(Cbz)-`. That's a piperazine ring. Wait, piperazine is `N1CCNCC1`.
